title: [3.13] gh-140471: Fix buffer overflow in AST node initialization with malformed `_fields` (GH-140506) (#140510)
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 97-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the trigger began (ABR BEGIN; no marker at the access in an upstream reproducer)) and completed with no fault; the trigger ended with EXIT 1

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc's blocks as child lifetimes (patch 0014, CDERIVE/CREVOKE; tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: reached (the trigger began (ABR BEGIN; no marker at the access in an upstream reproducer)) and completed with no fault; the trigger ended with EXIT 1

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial SILENT (spatial-20261006-131005); sublet DETECTED cause=5 (sublet-20261006-123446); cheribsd-revocation SILENT (boundary-20261007-020413)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-buffer-overflow (READ 4) at _copy_characters Objects/unicodeobject.c:1606. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.

pinned_measurement.method: five repeats on each of the three arms under PYTHONHASHSEED=0, on the pinned platform (capstone-qemu d35af47b, VM state /tmp/capstone/vm-pinned). Added because unpinned this case did not hold still. The virtual arms ran their configuration's controls before every repeat and the CheriBSD arm ran its si_code self-test before every repeat (bounds si_code=1, revoked si_code=2), so a silent arm is live and silent, not absent.

arms.virtual-nested-pools: CAUGHT cause=28 in memcpy x5, attributed by negative_control.py; the faulting pc differs only in the load base across the five (0x3f89002654, 0x3fb9002654, 0x3fab002654, 0x3f7f002654, 0x3f9f002654) -- one instruction

note: Pinned measurement supersedes the single unpinned run. (2) is a genuine detection: cause=28 CAP_OOB on the defective copy itself, five times out of five, with its negative control clean on the same image. (1) and (3) are silent five times out of five. The defect is a type confusion -- a bytes object read through the PyUnicode layout, so the copy's length comes out of the wrong field -- and the over-read that follows is what (2) rejects. See ~/cpython-false-positive-examples/02-same-bytes-two-meanings.c.
